usageNotes: Use this to define an IP subnet within an existing SDN VNet — a required step before VMs on that VNet can receive DHCP leases or participate in layer-3 routing. The caller must hold SDN.Allocate on '/sdn/zones/<zone>/<vnet>'; after creating the subnet, run 'apply' (POST /cluster/sdn) to push the configuration to nodes. The 'gateway' field is only meaningful on layer-3 zone VNets; setting 'snat' enables NAT masquerade via pve-firewall for outbound traffic from this subnet.

examples.summary: Create a /24 subnet with a gateway, DHCP range, and SNAT enabled on VNet 'tenant-vnet1'

tips: The 'subnet' identifier must match the pve-sdn-subnet-id format — typically CIDR notation such as '10.10.20.0/24'.
After creating or modifying SDN objects, call POST /cluster/sdn to apply pending changes cluster-wide; subnets are not active until applied.
DHCP ranges require the Proxmox IPAM integration (dnsmasq) to be configured on the zone; without it the range is stored but not served.
Setting 'snat' without pve-firewall enabled on the node has no effect — verify firewall is active before relying on masquerade.
